training.tooltip.means_lr_end: Controls how much Gaussian positions can still move near the end of training. Lower values make geometry settle down more; higher values let positions keep adapting late, but can cause drifting or instability.
training.tooltip.scaling_lr_end: Controls how much Gaussian sizes can still change near the end of training. Lower values stabilize final splat sizes; higher values let scale keep adapting late.
training.tooltip.cropbox_lr_scale: Controls how much splats outside the crop box still learn. Use low values to focus training inside the ROI; use higher values if outside context should still adapt. Only matters with an active crop box.
training.tooltip.cropbox_loss_weight: Controls how much image pixels outside the crop box affect training. Lower it to focus on the ROI; raise it when the surrounding scene should still influence the result. Only matters with an active crop box.
training.tooltip.normal_loss_space: Normal prior space: auto, camera-opencv, camera-opengl, or world
training.tooltip.growth_grad_threshold: Sets how strong a refinement signal must be before a splat can grow. Lower values allow more areas to grow; higher values focus growth only on stronger visible errors.
training.tooltip.grow_fraction: Controls how many eligible candidates grow each refine step. Increase it when the model needs capacity faster; decrease it when growth is too aggressive or noisy.
training.tooltip.opacity_decay: Gradually reduces opacity during refinement, strongest earlier in training. Increase it to help clear weak splats; lower it if useful surfaces fade.
training.tooltip.scale_decay: Gradually shrinks Gaussian scale during refinement, strongest earlier in training. Increase it to fight bloated splats; lower it if coverage becomes holey.
training.tooltip.means_noise_weight: Adds position exploration noise. Increase it when growth seems stuck or areas remain undercovered; lower it if geometry becomes noisy or unstable.
training.tooltip.bounds_percentile: Controls how scene bounds are estimated from Gaussian positions. Lower values ignore more outliers; higher values include more of the point distribution.
training.tooltip.use_error_map: Steers refinement toward image regions with visible reconstruction error. Turn it off if error-map guidance overreacts to noise or appearance mismatch.
training.tooltip.use_edge_map: Biases refinement toward image edges. Use it for sharper silhouettes and detail boundaries; turn it off if noisy edges or texture artifacts get too much capacity.
training.tooltip.far_scene_min_fraction: Controls when far-field features activate. Lower it to enable far-field handling more easily; raise it so it only activates when enough splats are truly far away.
training.tooltip.growth_ratio_rank: Helps rarely visible but high-error regions compete with frequently visible regions. Use it when distant or under-seen areas remain under-refined.
training.tooltip.growth_ratio_pow: Controls how strongly visibility count affects growth ranking. Higher values favor under-seen error regions more; lower values behave closer to raw error ranking.
training.tooltip.fill_pacing_iter: Spreads capacity growth over time instead of filling the model too early. `0` lets the cap fill as quickly as refinement allows.
training.tooltip.far_seed_dose: Controls extra far/background seeding. Increase it when distant backgrounds stay sparse; keep it low if far-field growth adds unnecessary splats.
training.tooltip.penalty_weight: Weight for opacity penalty in background regions
training.tooltip.step_scaling_unlocked: Manual: training parameters are not auto-scaled.
training.tooltip.opacity_reg: Penalizes opacity behavior. Use to discourage unwanted opacity buildup; keep low if it removes useful semi-transparent detail.
training.tooltip.scale_reg: Penalizes Gaussian scale. Use to reduce oversized splats or bloating; keep low if it hurts coverage.
training.tooltip.lambda_dssim: Blends pixel L1 loss with structural similarity. Increase for structure/perceptual similarity; decrease for stricter pixel color matching.
training.tooltip.tv_loss_weight: Smooths bilateral-grid corrections. Use with Bilateral Grid to avoid noisy local color correction; irrelevant when the grid is off.
training.tooltip.refine_every: How often training adds/splits/prunes Gaussians. Lower values refine more often but cost more; higher values make refinement less frequent.
training.tooltip.start_refine: When adaptive refinement begins. Delay it if the initial model needs time to stabilize before adding/removing splats.
training.tooltip.stop_refine: When refinement ends. Use earlier stops for faster, more stable final polishing; later stops for scenes needing more capacity.
training.tooltip.morton_reorder_interval: Periodically reorganizes Gaussians in memory by spatial location. It does not change the scene directly; it helps performance after many grow/split operations have scrambled internal order. Set to `0` to disable.
training.tooltip.grow_until_iter: MRNF-specific cutoff for adding new Gaussians. Use later values when details are still missing; earlier values to stop growth sooner.
training.tooltip.reset_every: Periodically resets opacity to help pruning/refinement escape bad opacity states. Use carefully; too frequent resets can disrupt convergence.
training.tooltip.sh_upgrade_every: How often SH Bands color expressiveness increases. Use slower upgrades when geometry/color need to stabilize first.
training.tooltip.init_opacity: Sets how visible the initial Gaussians are when training starts. Higher values make the starting splats more opaque and can fill the scene faster, but may create opacity buildup or floaters. Lower values start more transparent and conservative, but may take longer to form solid surfaces.
training.tooltip.init_scaling: Sets the starting size of the initial Gaussians. Higher values make splats cover more area at the start, which can help fill sparse scenes but may cause blurry blobs. Lower values start smaller and more precise, but may leave gaps or require more refinement.
training.tooltip.random_init: Starts from randomly generated points instead of the dataset's SfM/COLMAP sparse point cloud. Use when the point cloud is missing, broken, or unhelpful; keep it off when the dataset has a good sparse point cloud, because that usually gives training a better starting shape.
training.tooltip.extent: Bounding box size for random init
training.tooltip.resize_factor: Controls training image resolution. Use larger downsampling when VRAM is tight or previews matter more than detail; use 1 for full resolution, 2 for half resolution, 4 for quarter resolution
training.tooltip.max_width: Caps the image width before training. Use it to keep memory and speed predictable on very large photos; keep 0 to preserve native size.
training.tooltip.cpu_cache: Store decoded images in system memory. Use when you have enough RAM and want less disk/decode overhead during training.
training.tooltip.use_16bit_color: Preserves high bit-depth/HDR color input. Use for HDR or high dynamic range datasets; avoid if memory/cache size matters more.
training.tooltip.test_every: Chooses how many images are held out for evaluation. Use a smaller value for more validation coverage, larger for more training images.
training.tooltip.enable_eval: Runs quality metrics on held-out images. Use when you want measurable validation during training; disable for fastest runs.
training.tooltip.save_steps: Iterations at which to save checkpoints AND run evaluation (if Enable Eval is checked). Evaluation always runs at the same iterations as checkpoints.
training.tooltip.lr_position: Controls how fast Gaussian centers move. Increase only if geometry adapts too slowly; lower if training becomes unstable or noisy.
training.tooltip.lr_sh_coeff: Controls how fast view-dependent color learns. Tune when color/view effects lag or flicker.
training.tooltip.lr_opacity: Controls transparency learning. Use higher values for faster opacity cleanup, lower values if opacity changes become unstable.
training.tooltip.lr_scaling: Controls splat size adaptation. Raise for faster shape/coverage changes; lower if splats grow or shrink erratically.
training.tooltip.lr_rotation: Controls orientation updates for anisotropic Gaussians. Tune when elongated splats orient too slowly or become unstable.
training.tooltip.btn_stop: End training and keep current result
training.tooltip.opt.depth_loss_mode.ssi: Auto-detect per image whether the prior is disparity-like or depth-like
training.tooltip.opt.depth_loss_mode.ssi_disparit: Prior is disparity-like (larger = closer), e.g. Depth Anything or MiDaS output
training.tooltip.opt.depth_loss_mode.ssi_depth: Prior is depth-like (larger = farther), e.g. metric depth models

tooltip.btn_switch_edit: Switch to edit mode for the trained scene
tooltip.ppisp_exposure_from_exif: Initializes PPISP exposure from camera metadata. Use when EXIF exposure values are present and trustworthy.
tooltip.ppisp_freeze_from_sidecar: Loads existing PPISP correction data instead of learning it from scratch. Use when reusing calibration from a previous run or imported sidecar.
tooltip.ppisp_sidecar_path: The file path for frozen PPISP data. Use when Frozen Sidecar is enabled and you need to point training at the saved PPISP weights.
tooltip.ppisp_sidecar_browse: Browse for a PPISP sidecar file
tooltip.bg_color: The fixed background color for Color or Modulation mode. Use when training should assume a specific backdrop, commonly black, white, or a sampled scene color.
tooltip.bg_image_path: A custom background image for training. Use when the scene should be optimized against a known background plate.
tooltip.dataset_path: The dataset root currently used for training.
tooltip.dataset_images: The image directory inside the dataset.
tooltip.dataset_output: Path where checkpoints and trained artifacts are written. Use it to verify the run will save to the intended project/output folder.
tooltip.opt_strategy_display: Shows the active growth/pruning strategy. Use it to understand which refinement controls below actually apply.
tooltip.bilateral_grid_x: Controls how many correction cells the grid has horizontally. Increase it if the correction needs to vary more across the image from left to right; lower it for smoother, cheaper correction with less risk of patchy local color changes. Only applies when Bilateral Grid or Exposure Correction is enabled.
tooltip.bilateral_grid_y: Controls how many correction cells the grid has vertically. Increase it if different parts of the image need different correction; lower it if the correction becomes noisy, patchy, or too detailed. Only applies when Bilateral Grid or Exposure Correction is enabled.
tooltip.bilateral_grid_w: Controls how many brightness/appearance levels the grid can distinguish. Increase it when dark and bright areas need different corrections; lower it for smoother behavior and less overfitting. Only applies when Bilateral Grid or Exposure Correction is enabled.
tooltip.bilateral_grid_lr: Controls how quickly the grid learns color/appearance correction. Increase it if correction is too slow or too weak; decrease it if colors shift too aggressively, flicker, or become unstable. Only applies when Bilateral Grid or Exposure Correction is enabled.
tooltip.prune_opacity: IGS+ pruning threshold. Raise to remove weak splats more aggressively; lower to keep faint/detail splats.
tooltip.min_opacity: Controls when faint Gaussians are considered too transparent to keep. Raise it to clean up weak floating splats more aggressively; lower it to preserve faint detail.
tooltip.sparsify_steps: Adds this many extra sparsity-optimization steps after normal training. More steps give the model more time to adapt before pruning; fewer steps finish faster but may hurt quality more. Only applies when Sparsity is enabled.
tooltip.init_rho: Controls how strongly the sparsity phase pushes weak/low-opacity Gaussians toward removal. Increase it for stronger compression pressure; lower it if the model loses detail or quality too quickly. Only applies when Sparsity is enabled.
tooltip.prune_ratio: Sets the final fraction of Gaussians removed after the sparsity phase. Higher values make the result smaller and faster but can remove detail; lower values preserve more quality but compress less. Pruning is based on the lowest-opacity Gaussians. Only applies when Sparsity is enabled.

sh_degree.0: Diffuse only — fastest, no view-dependent color
sh_degree.3: Third-order SH — best quality, most VRAM

mask_mode.none: Train on the entire image, no masking
mask_mode.segment: Use the segmentation mask for foreground
mask_mode.ignore: Ignore masked pixels in the loss
mask_mode.alpha_consistent: Enforce alpha consistency with the mask

densify_error_map.ssim: Full SSIM densify error, including brightness mismatches
densify_error_map.ssim_cs: Contrast and structure only; ignore brightness-only mismatches

bg_mode.color: Use the selected fixed background color. Best when the dataset has a known, consistent background or you want predictable training.
bg_mode.modulation: Vary a solid RGB background over training steps using sinusoidal colors. Use when empty or transparent regions should not settle on one fixed color, but full noise would be too aggressive.
bg_mode.image: Use the selected background image. Best when training should match a known background plate.
bg_mode.random: Generate a per-pixel RGB noise background each step. Use when you strongly want to prevent transparent regions from fitting any fixed background.

tooltip.exposure_correction: A newer appearance correction system for exposure, white balance, and local color differences between photos. Use when images vary in brightness, color, or lighting; it replaces Bilateral Grid and PPISP.
tooltip.exposure_correction_grid_start: Controls when Exposure Correction’s local residual grid starts learning. A later start lets global exposure and white balance settle first. Lower it only when local lighting or color differences need correction earlier. Only applies to Exposure Correction, not standalone Bilateral Grid.
tooltip.bilateral_grid: A per-photo grid that compensates for local exposure/color differences during training. Use only when you specifically want the older standalone correction path instead of Exposure Correction.
tooltip.ppisp: A physically based per-camera/per-photo appearance model for exposure, vignetting, white balance, and tone curve. Use when you need detailed camera appearance correction and are not using Exposure Correction.
tooltip.ppisp_warmup: Controls how long PPISP takes to reach full learning speed. Use more warmup so geometry and base color stabilize before strong appearance correction; use less if PPISP should respond earlier. Only affects training when PPISP or Exposure Correction is enabled.
tooltip.ppisp_reg: Keeps standalone PPISP corrections from drifting too far away from neutral camera behavior. Increase it if PPISP starts absorbing scene color or hiding reconstruction issues; lower it if PPISP cannot correct real camera appearance differences. Only affects training with standalone PPISP, not Exposure Correction.
tooltip.densify_error_map: Chooses which image-error signal guides densification. Use SSIM to grow from all visible differences, including brightness; use Contrast-Structure to focus growth on edges/shapes and avoid spending Gaussians on brightness-only mismatches such as sky or exposure differences.
tooltip.max_screen_share: Sets the screen-size cap for each Gaussian. Lower it to prevent oversized splats, blurry blobs, or false sheet-like surfaces from covering too much of the view; raise it when broad real surfaces need larger splats. 0 or 1 disables the cap.
tooltip.screen_share_penalty: Controls how strongly oversized screen-space splats are pushed to shrink. Increase it when large splats take over; lower it if important broad surfaces collapse.
tooltip.oversize_split_fraction: Reserves part of growth for splitting splats that are too large on screen. Use it when big sheets or blobs should be broken into smaller pieces instead of only shrunk.
tooltip.strategy: The main training strategy that decides how Gaussians are added, refined, or pruned. Use MRNF as the default; use MCMC or IGS+ when comparing training behavior or solving strategy-specific cases.
tooltip.iterations: The planned number of optimization steps. In Auto mode, the schedule uses roughly 100 iterations per active training image, with a minimum of 30,000 iterations. Use more for complex scenes or cleaner convergence; use fewer for quick previews.
tooltip.max_gaussians: The upper limit on model size. Raise it for more scene detail if VRAM allows; lower it to reduce memory use, training cost, and output size.
tooltip.background_improvements: An MRNF enhancement bundle for far-away/background areas. Use it for outdoor scenes, skies, distant buildings, or backgrounds that look sparse, blurry, or underfit.
tooltip.sh_degree: Controls how much view-dependent color each Gaussian can represent. Use 3 for best quality; use lower values for faster training, lower VRAM use, or mostly diffuse scenes.
tooltip.mask_mode: Controls how masks affect training loss and opacity. Use when your dataset has object/background masks and you want to isolate the subject, ignore unwanted areas, or enforce alpha behavior.
tooltip.use_depth_loss: Adds scale/shift-invariant depth-map guidance to geometry learning. Use when reliable depth priors can improve relative structure, depth ordering, or surface placement.
tooltip.depth_loss_mode: Tells depth loss whether the prior behaves like depth or disparity. Use Auto unless you know the source model's convention.
tooltip.depth_loss_weight: Controls how strongly depth supervision affects training. Increase when geometry is unstable; decrease when depth maps are noisy or hurt visual quality.
tooltip.use_normal_loss: Adds surface-orientation guidance from normal maps. Use when clean geometry, flatter surfaces, or surface consistency matter more than purely photometric reconstruction.
tooltip.normal_auto_generate: Automatically creates normal maps with MoGe-2 when compatible maps are missing or the wrong size. Use when you want normal supervision but do not already have compatible normal maps.
tooltip.normal_loss_weight: Controls the strength of normal-map supervision. Increase for stronger surface orientation guidance; lower it if normals cause smoothing or artifacts.
tooltip.normal_consistency_weight: Encourages rendered normals and rendered depth to agree. Use when surfaces look geometrically inconsistent.
tooltip.normal_flatten_weight: Encourages splats to become flatter and more surface-like while normal supervision is active. Use for cleaner surfaces; reduce it if the model becomes brittle or overly thin.
tooltip.normal_start_fraction: Delays normal supervision until partway through training. Use it to let the base image fit stabilize before normals influence geometry.
tooltip.normal_end_fraction: Stops normal supervision before the end of training. Use when normals help early structure but interfere with final visual polish.
tooltip.sparsity: Adds a pruning/compression phase. Use when the trained model is too large or slow and you can trade a bit of quality for size or performance.
tooltip.gut: Enables 3DGUT-style training/rendering for distorted camera models. Use for datasets with non-pinhole cameras or lens distortion that should remain part of the camera model. Note that most viewers do not support rendering splats trained with this mode.
tooltip.undistort: Applies lens undistortion during training. Use when your input images are distorted and you want training to correct them on the fly instead of using distortion-aware rendering.
tooltip.mip_filter: Applies anti-aliasing during training. Use for scenes with fine textures, repeated patterns, or shimmer/aliasing artifacts. For best viewing results, enable anti-aliasing when viewing the final render too.
tooltip.ppisp_controller: Trains a neural controller to generalize PPISP correction to new views. Use when corrected appearance should hold up outside the original camera views.
tooltip.ppisp_activation_step: Decides when PPISP controller training starts. Use a late step so the base Gaussian model is stable before controller distillation begins.
tooltip.ppisp_controller_lr: Controls how fast the PPISP controller learns. Tune if controller training is too slow, unstable, or overpowering.
tooltip.ppisp_freeze_gaussians: Locks the Gaussian model while the PPISP controller learns. Use during controller distillation so the target appearance stays stable.
tooltip.ppisp_lr: Controls how quickly PPISP appearance correction learns exposure, vignetting, color, and tone adjustments. Increase it if correction reacts too slowly; decrease it if appearance changes become unstable. Only affects training when PPISP or Exposure Correction is enabled.
tooltip.bg_modulation: Chooses how the training background is supplied behind transparent or empty pixels. Color uses the selected fixed background color. Modulation varies a solid RGB background over training steps using sinusoidal colors. Image uses a selected background image. Random generates a different per-pixel RGB noise background each step.
tooltip.invert_masks: Reverses mask meaning. Use when your black-and-white masks use the opposite color for the masked region.
tooltip.use_alpha_as_mask: Uses image transparency as the training mask. Use when RGBA images already contain the mask and no separate mask files are needed.
tooltip.steps_scaler: Scales step-based training settings together. Auto mode uses roughly 100 iterations per active training image, with a minimum of 30,000 iterations.
